question_text: Find the period of f(x) = |sin x|.

mark_split.label: State that π is the least period

Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The split gives one mark to showing that f(x + π) = f(x) and one to ruling out any smaller positive number, which is what makes π the period rather than only a period. recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Show that f(x + π) = f(x)
steps.margin_note: First mark. sin x repeats after 2π, but the modulus turns the negative half of the wave upward, so the shape repeats after only π.
steps.memory_tip: The modulus turns the negative half up, so |sin x| repeats twice as often as sin x: 2π becomes π.
lines: So π is a period of f.

recall.must_convey: That sin(x + π) = −sin x, so |sin(x + π)| = |sin x| and π is a period of |sin x|.
accept: sin of x plus pi is minus sin x so the modulus makes them equal
shifting by pi changes only the sign and the modulus removes it
f of x plus pi equals f of x so pi is a period
sin x plus pi ante minus sin x, modulus tho sign pothundi
the modulus makes the shifted value the same

steps.why: The modulus does not change the size, only the sign. Since sin(x + π) is exactly −sin x, taking the modulus removes the only difference between the two halves.
common_mistakes: Answering 2π, the period of sin x, without using the modulus.
Writing sin(x + π) = sin x, which drops the minus sign.

steps.label: State that π is the least period
steps.margin_note: Second mark. π is not only a period, it is the smallest one: |sin x| is 0 at x = 0 and stays above 0 for every x between 0 and π.
steps.memory_tip: Check the least period from the zeros: |sin x| is 0 at x = 0 and next 0 at x = π, so nothing smaller works.
lines: |sin x| = 0 at x = 0, and |sin x| > 0 for
So no positive number smaller than π can

recall.must_convey: That π is the least positive period, because |sin x| is zero at x = 0 and positive throughout 0 < x < π.
accept: pi is the smallest period because the zeros are pi apart
the modulus halves the period from two pi to pi
no number smaller than pi repeats the values
period pi, zeros madhya duram pi kabatti

steps.why: The period means the SMALLEST positive repeat, so f(x + π) = f(x) on its own is not the full answer. The zeros are the quickest way to rule out anything shorter.
common_mistakes: Stopping after f(x + π) = f(x) without saying π is the least period.
Giving π/2, which is the period of |sin 2x|, not of |sin x|.
